reading:
The panels love this line for its system. It works as a page template and not as a palette: one real cased terminal stands beside a matte desk, and it is the only lit, rounded thing on the page. Every page opens on a head row, and every filter is a latched key with an LED. Each page's glass draws that page's own data: ASCII late bars on To do, the moving-coil spend needle on Status, the radar on Ideas. The warm-up from a bright line and the question typed on the glass gave it the round's truest return of the tube (soul 8.8, interaction 8.8, main r13 #1 at 8.33).

On the tour's landing panel it fell to 7.54, behind four tour finals, for three reasons:
- **The title.** "What's on your mind?" says nothing of the job, and its 40px VT323 tall-tick apostrophe has drawn complaints three rounds running.
- **A dashboard, not a world.** The desk is a stack of equal-weight boxed bands with ringed numbers and many small tracked capitals. It has almost no line language, and machine and desk do not touch: there is a 290-700px dead void under Home's terminal, and the green pool spilling onto the desk was lost.
- **Small type faults that keep coming back.** Whole phrases are set in letterspaced mono ("was due 5 days ago"). The Plans trace's numerals collide. Plans has no primary, and Vera appears three times on Chat. On the phone, Chat opens on the terminal, so the thread starts below the first screen.

The tour finals that beat it won with three things:
- Sill Line's lit stem from the Next up tube into Coming up's rail (feedback 9.1, "the best single gesture"), which joins machine and page.
- One-strip setup with a short track and one action.
- To do's ring stop that is the tick you press, under a due margin set in sans.

Two of their smaller devices were also praised: Departures' 'usually Plans' starters and its one-line Status answer, and Lit Manual's round countdown dial.

To win, this line has to:
- keep the machine-beside-desk law and the glass light;
- physically connect the terminal to the desk;
- take the line language in where it does work;
- put a job word in a real headline;
- shed the dashboard boxes and the mono phrases;
- fit the 200k budget, which the parent has nearly spent (195.9k).

briefs.name: Desk Terminal, Patched
briefs.hypothesis: Joined lost the landing panel on three counts: a title that says nothing of the job, machine and desk that never touch (the void under the terminal, no line language), and a desk that read as a generic dashboard. Its system, light and controls were never the problem. This cross patches the terminal into the desk with a lit lead into Coming up's rail, the tour's best-scored gesture rebuilt as a cable from a cased machine. It gives the glass a job-word headline with no apostrophe to break, and swaps the boxed, ringed bands for rails whose stops are the controls, with sans due margins. It keeps every element its judges scored 8.5+ (head row, latched keys, glass per page, needle meter, warm-up) and adds the three devices that lifted the tour finals past it. It should beat the carried design on the soul, style and type lenses without giving back interaction or usability.
briefs.brief:
Start from r13-idea-1's files (palette .json, variants/r13-idea-1/: sheet.css, templates, tokens.json). Keep the law: one cased, lit terminal on the left of every page holds the tube, its deck of latched keys and the status foot, and a square matte slate desk holds only the family's rows.

0. BUDGET FIRST. sheet.css is 195,964 of 200,000 characters. Before adding anything:
- Strip every comment from sheet.css. The parent keeps today's long explanatory comments; this alone frees well over 20k.
- Delete the cobalt corner wash: the `--wash` token, the washGlow rules and any `radial-gradient` that uses --wash. Set tokens.json washGlow to 0.
- Delete the fading row-afterglow transitions on rows; see 9.
- Delete the Plans day-number trace; see 6.
- Delete the numbered band rings on Home; see 3.
- Delete the Contents plate on any page with five bands or fewer.
Target about 175k before the grafts land.

1. THE CASE. Thin it:
- Radius 6px (was the round slab).
- A 2px graphite bezel (#2c3135) with a 1px hairline lip (inset 0 1px 0 #ffffff0f).
- No outer cobalt glow.
- The glass keeps E12-E15 at full strength: halo, bloom, scanlines, the warm-up from a bright line (E16), and the breathing power lamp (E20).
- `.bench > .terminal` stays sticky at `top: calc(var(--bar-h) + 1rem); max-height: calc(100dvh - var(--bar-h) - 2rem)`. Remove its `overflow-y:auto`: every page's terminal must fit by content. No inner scroll anywhere.

2. HOME'S TERMINAL (widen it to 30rem on Home only, `.page-home .bench{grid-template-columns:30rem minmax(0,1fr)}`).

The glass, top to bottom:
- The scrollback row: her screen glyph (E19) at 1.5rem, then 'VERA · FRI 2 OCT' in VT323 at the cell size.
- NEXT UP in inverse, the plan name bright and its when-line, beside a small 5.5rem radar (E17, sweep kept).
- '› 4 more after Next up' as the link, ending the off-by-one.
- A dashed glass rule.
- THE HEADLINE (see the title field) as the page's h1 and the textarea's label. Set it in 'IBM Plex Sans Condensed' 600, 2.5rem/1.02, -0.012em, text-wrap:balance, colour #a9eec0 (the glass's mid strength) with E13's soft text bloom. Only 'plan' is #6dff9c with E1's two-layer halo and a white-hot core (colour #eafff1, text-shadow 0 0 .08em #fff, 0 0 .35em #6dff9c, 0 0 1em #6dff9c66). A slow E15 block cursor follows it; it is the only blinker on Home, so the bar's cursor stands still.
- The box, as the tube's last rows: a green-black glass field (#06100b, 1px #2f4a3a edge) at least 3 rows. It is led by L095's lit prompt '›' in Plex Mono 500 #6dff9c with an 8px bloom, in its own flex cell (`.prompt-line`, aria-hidden). On :focus-within the field takes E4 (border #6dff9c, 0 12px 22px -16px #6dff9ce6 underglow). The family's words stay in Plex Sans 1.0625rem ink, never VT323.

The deck (graphite keyboard ledge under the glass):
- Row 1: FROM select, then the mic, then Send, immediately under the field on desktop and phone alike; this kills the 100px bezel gap on the phone. 'Send where I am' is the checkbox at the row's end, wrapping only on the phone.
- Row 2: the three ways to start as a 2-up grid of keys with 0.5rem gaps (`.starters{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:.5rem}`; the third spans both). Each key is a 2-line plate: the starter in Plex Sans 500 ink, under it 'usually Plans' / 'usually To do' / 'usually Ideas' in .8125rem dim.

The foot:
- The Ready lamp, then Departures' one-line answer in Plex Sans: '5 working · 1 needs a look · $0.00 of $2.00 today', with 'needs a look' an amber link to Status.
- On Status itself the foot drops its 'Status →'.

3. HOME'S DESK, re-ordered so Coming up comes first. Band heads lose their numbered rings: each is a Plex Sans Condensed 600 1.5rem title, then its figure set inline in Plex Sans tabular ('4 coming', '4 open · 3 late'), then its links at the right ('All plans →'). A 2px cap of bone (#d4cfc4 at 40%) sits over each head; section colour stays in icons only.

(a) COMING UP, with THE PATCH LEAD (graft 1):
- A lit 2px #6dff9c lead (with a 1px #eafff1 hot core) leaves the terminal case's right edge through a 10px socket ring drawn on the case at the NEXT UP row.
- It crosses the gutter and lands in the NOW lamp at the head of Coming up's rail.
- The rail is steel #58697a with ring stops per plan; its first stretch from NOW to stop one is lit.
- Build the lead as `.coming::before` extending left by the gutter width at the rail's y (no wrapper markup), with E12's spill: a 70px radial pool of #6dff9c1a at the socket, so the machine lights the desk under it.
- Rows: date set on the digit (bold day numeral, weekday and month in bone, never denim), name, dotted leader capped at 46rem, time in Plex Mono tabular, 'in 7 days' in Plex Sans dim.

(b) SETUP AS ONE STRIP (graft 2):
- A slate strip, 3.5rem high, with the four-signal 'needs a look' 2px amber left edge.
- 'Finish setting up', then a short steel track of three 44px ring stops: steel rings, the next step's ring lit #6dff9c with a halo. It ends in a T buffer.
- 'All 3 steps' as a link, then 'Next: choose your own password →' at the right.

(c) TO DO ON A TICK LINE (graft 3):
- Each task hangs from a steel rail whose ring stop IS the tick button: a 2.75rem hit area, 1.15rem ring, amber ring when late, dashed when undated. Hover fills it sage, press lights it #6dff9c.
- A left due margin, 8.5rem and right-aligned, in Plex Sans 13px tabular: the absolute date in 500 ink, then 'was due 5 days ago' in 500 amber. This replaces the letterspaced mono due column.
- WHO stays as a right column.
- The lit NOW run crosses between the late and upcoming rows, its head white-hot.
- '3 late' in the head is the amber link to `tasks?status=late`.

(d) LATELY ADDED and (e) THE KIDS' WISHES keep their one-line rows; the kind colour lives only in the kind icon's ring. 'Something to eat' becomes a last row of Lately added rather than its own card.

4. FOUR SIGNALS EVERYWHERE (this line's own Mapped fix):
- on = lit #6dff9c lamp with halo;
- waiting = steel dot;
- off/unset = pewter ring (#7a8590);
- needs a look = amber 2px bar.
Red (#ff6b6b) only for something that has stopped. Status's contents plate and Settings carry a one-line legend of the four shapes, so 'no key' stops reading as an alarm.

5. EVERY INNER PAGE keeps Joined's head row:
- icon, then the h1 raised to Plex Sans Condensed 600 2.75rem;
- the lede on the title's line at ≥80rem;
- the one green primary at the right (E3 glow kept).
Plans gains its primary, 'Add a plan', which targets the existing add fold the way To do's does. Pages with nothing live (the form, Wishes, Family, Memory, an idea's page) fold the terminal to its one-line Ready foot under the head row, and the desk takes the full width.

6. PLANS. The glass's crowded day-number trace becomes LIT MANUAL'S ROUND COUNTDOWN DIAL (graft 4):
- a round tube 15rem across, in this line's graphite case with the 2px bezel;
- a ring of 28 ticks (four weeks) with now at the top, and a lit tick with a halo on each day that has a plan;
- in the centre, VT323 'Next in' / a 3.5rem '2' / 'days', and 'then 3 more' dim;
- E14 scanlines and E17's slow sweep from now to the next plan.
Under it, the View and Month latched keys stay. Month cells: plan chips never break inside a word (`overflow-wrap:normal; hyphens:manual; text-wrap:balance`, with 0.875rem names). The weekend columns are a step warmer slate (#141b20); today's cell is a #6dff9c outline with a small halo.

7. TO DO PAGE:
- the same tick line as 3(c), at full width;
- the glass keeps the ASCII Late/This week/Later/No date bars, each row a link to its filter;
- 'Edit or snooze' keeps its words.

8. IDEAS (this line's Mapped fix):
- The tube plots the family's places round a lit home: blips at their bearing and drive time, numbered to the list.
- Each blip is an `<a>` to its row with a 44px hit area (not aria-hidden). Labels are VT323 ≥18px, with collision offsets and a leader for the three downtown places. At most two ring labels.
- Kind stays the 3-up latched bank at 2.75rem. For is a second row of short keys. Status is the third row, inside a `<details>` titled 'Status: any but dropped'.
- The terminal must end inside 900px.

9. ROWS:
- Drop the fading afterglow. Rows get a steady pointer-only hover: a #6dff9c14 wash and a 2px inset sage (#86d9a6) left edge, `@media (hover:hover)` only, so a parked mouse never reads as a selection.
- Focus keeps E5's 2px #6dff9c ring.

10. CHAT:
- Her screen leaves the terminal. On Chat the terminal holds the conversations as its Contents (one row each, a lamp for a waiting turn) and the Ready foot.
- Her mark stays beside her lines.
- On the phone, the thread comes first in the DOM, then the sticky box, then the terminal folded to its Ready line. Reorder the DOM, not CSS order.

11. STATUS:
- The moving-coil needle keeps its hot needle and hatched overrun.
- Add a lit limit tick at $2.00 and the ghost needle at the 30-day average, labelled.
- The h1's lede becomes the one-line answer ('5 working · 1 needs a look · $0.00 of $2.00 today').
- The contents plate shows the four-signal shapes beside each row's figure.

12. PHONE (390px). Home: the glass and headline first (the headline at clamp(2rem, 8.4vw, 2.5rem), two lines), then the deck and its 2-up starters, then the desk with the lead dropped and the rail kept. No sideways scroll anywhere. The DOM order matches the drawing on every page.

briefs.avoids:
- It answers 'What's on your mind?' says nothing of the job (landing panel feedback, skeptic and the owner) and the VT323 tall-tick apostrophe (every lens).
- It answers 'more dashboard than a world' and 'Home stacks equal-weight cards' (landing panel system, style). Home's bands lose their boxes and rings, and the desk gains rails whose stops are the controls.
- It answers 'tubes all one size and shape, templated' (soul). Plans gets a round dial, Ideas a map, To do bars, Status a needle and Home a scrollback glass.
- It answers 'many small tracked capitals' and 'mono-heavy rows lean toward an editor theme' (landing panel type, skeptic, usability). Due phrases and figures go to sans, and mono is kept to times.
- It answers the dead void, the heavy case, the touching chips, Send far from the field on the phone, Vera thrice on Chat, the off-by-one, the denim months, the colliding Plans trace numerals, the missing Plans primary and the invisible afterglow.
- It avoids the tour's own faults: amber doing two jobs (setup is steel with an amber edge), the subway-map overload (one lead and three rails, not lines on every page), the sideways-scrolling starters on the phone (2-up grid), and costume enamel starter tints (the starters stay graphite keys).
- It gives up the Contents plate on pages with five bands or fewer, the Plans ASCII trace, the numbered band rings, the full-height VT323 question, the cobalt wash and the row afterglow fade.
briefs.title: Give Vera something to *plan*. Not yet tried in the tour or the crossing rounds; this line has only carried the failed 'What's on your mind?'. It keeps what the judges ranked best in 'Tell Vera what to plan.': it names who hears you, it invites the family to tell her something, and it ends on the lit job word where the eye stops. It fixes that title's two faults. 'Tell Vera what to plan' can read as if she does the planning; here the family hands her something. 'What's our plan?' can read as 'show me the plan'; this cannot. And unlike 'Anything to plan?' it cannot be answered 'no'. 'Something' takes in a weekend, a reminder, an idea to keep and a wish alike. With no apostrophe, it can never break on the glass. It sets as the terminal's own prompt: Plex Sans Condensed on lit glass, 'plan' white-hot under E1's halo, then the block cursor.
